newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's dollar ends weaker, nearing two-year low.
newsitem.headline: Canada's dollar ends weaker, nearing two-year low.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended weaker on Monday at C$1.3849 (US$0.7220) from today's open of C$1.3798 (US$0.7247), hovering near a two-year low of C$1.3851 (US$0.7219).
* Dealers said nervous investors pushed the dollar weaker amid speculation of further U.S. rate hikes in May and tumbling Toronto stocks as a result of the Bre-X Minerals Ltd saga.
Dealers said the only interest in buying the Canadian dollar has come from sporadic orders by the Bank of Canada and Canadian exporters buying Canada dollars.

They said last week's hike in U.S. interest rates increased pressure on the Canadian dollar as interest rate spreads between Canada and the U.S. grew wider and speculation that more U.S. rate rises are in the offing for May.

"The Fed tightened 25 basis points and the (Canada) dollar continued to weaken as people focused on the timing of the next move because it is widely believed they will go another 25 (basis) points," Wateridge said.
